mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5% for three consecutive months, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% for 3 months, or the Rank IC over 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in CPI inflation and a rise in the federal funds rate signals an aggressive monetary policy response to inflation, which typically leads to negative equity returns as the real cost of capital rises and growth expectations decline over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (CPIAUCSL rising and FEDFUNDS rising) fails to predict negative returns in more than 55% of cases over a 5-year rolling window, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.0%), labor market tightness drives wage growth and corporate profit margins, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE is below 4.0%, or the Rank IC over 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1700.0 thousand units for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening in the residential construction sector, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence deteriorates.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when HOUST is below 1700.0 for 2 months, or the Rank IC over 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in residential investment (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based contraction in the housing sector, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the economy faces reduced consumer spending and investment.
failure_condition: The joint signal (RSAFS declining and HOUST declining) fails to predict negative returns in more than 55% of cases over a 5-year rolling window, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of strong industrial production growth (INDPRO > 105.0), manufacturing output expansion supports corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO exceeds 105.0, or the Rank IC over 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Higher levels of non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicate stronger labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC between PAYEMS and 60-day SPX returns is below 0.05 over any 5-year rolling window.
